why: Story 7.8 / ADR-009, AC4 and AC7: the file surface's FAIL direction, and what an absence means per source, through the real binary. Five criteria are decided by reading the tree and nothing else. E1-01 (a README exists) is a satisfied existence check. E1-02 (a changelog exists) is a FAILED existence check: the file is missing, which an existence read reports as the value false, and expected 'true' is not met. E1-03 (the README documents installation) is a content match. E1-04 (the migration guide has no TODO markers) is the case a careless surface gets wrong: the guide does not exist, and a content read of a missing file is unsatisfied for EVERY comparison including notContains -- text that does not exist cannot meet an expectation about text -- so it FAILS rather than passing vacuously; the stderrContains line pins that the report says so in words. E1-05 (the legacy config was removed) is the mirror of E1-02: an existence read expecting 'false' on a missing path PASSES, because for existence an absence is a value. So the fixture pins both halves of the rule in one run: absence is a fact for exists, and a failure for content. Verdict FAIL at exit 1 and never 3: every read succeeded, nothing was unreadable, so this is a product verdict about the branch and must not surface as infrastructure.
